title: Agarose Fluid Gels Formed by Shear Processing During Gelation for Suspended 3D Bioprinting
protocol: Prepare 1,000 mL of dispersed agarose by adding 5 g of agarose powder to ultrapure water in a 2,000 mL glass bottle.
Add a magnetic stirrer bar and secure the bottle cap by tightening and then loosening it by a quarter turn.
Autoclave the mixture for 15 min at 121 °C and 1 Bar.
Place the bottle on an unheated magnetic stirrer once cooled to 80 °C, stirring at 800 rpm.
Cool the sol until its temperature is lower than 32 °C while maintaining constant stirring.
Store the fluid gel at 4 °C.
Weigh out 0.5 g of low acyl gellan gum into a weighing boat.
Add 49.5 g of ultrapure water and a magnetic stirrer bar to a 100 mL glass bottle.
Fold the weighing boat containing gellan power in half.
Add the gellan powder to the water slowly while constantly stirring.
Sterilize the sol using an autoclave.
Allow the sol to cool to 20 °C.
Store the bioink at 4 °C until further use.
Prepare stock 5% (w/v) low-methoxy pectin solutions by weighing out 2.5 g of pectin powder into a weighing boat.
Add 50 mL of ultrapure water to a 100 mL glass bottle along with a magnetic stirrer.
Fold the weighing boat containing pectin power in half.
Add the pectin powder to the water slowly while constantly stirring.
Autoclave the aqueous mixture.
Cool the mixture to 20 °C.
Prepare 1:1 and 2:1 pectin-collagen blends by adding 3 mL of pectin solution to 3 mL of collagen solution or by adding 4 mL of pectin solution to 2 mL of collagen solution, respectively.
Gently mix the blends using a pipette, withdrawing and dispensing the mixture 10 times.
Store at 4 °C until further use.
Weigh out 2 g of alginate powder into a weighing boat.
Add 50 mL of ultrapure water to a 100 mL glass bottle along with a magnetic stirrer.
Fold the weighing boat containing alginate powder in half and add the powder slowly to the water while stirring constantly.
Heat the dispersion to 60 °C under constant stirring until the alginate is fully dissolved.
Cool the solution to 20 °C.
Dilute the alginate solution with Dulbecco's modified eagle medium (DMEM) by adding 25 mL of the alginate solution to 25 mL of DMEM.
Prepare alginate-collagen blends (1:1) by mixing 3 mL of the alginate/DMEM solution with 3 mL of collagen solution using a pipette, withdrawing and dispensing the mixture 10 times.
Store the alginate-collagen blend at 4 °C.
Turn on the rheometer and insert 40 mm serrated geometries.
Allow the system to stand for 30 min.
Zero the gap height of the rheometer using the zero-gap height function.
Add approximately 2 mL of sample onto the bottom plate.
Lower the top geometry to create a gap height of 1 mm.
Trim excess material expelled from between the plates by pulling it away with a flat, non-abrasive edge and soaking it up with tissue paper.
Undertake viscometry profiles to determine the injectability of the bioink.
Select viscometry test from the user options.
Input parameters for a shear rate-controlled ramp test: 0.1 to 500 s-1, with a 1 min ramp time.
Repeat the viscometry ramp test on new samples under stress control using upper and lower stresses determined from the shear rate-controlled ramp test.
Undertake small deformation tests to determine the gelling characteristics of the bioink.
Select oscillatory testing from the user options.
Input parameters into a single frequency test under constant strain: frequency 1 Hz, strain 0.5% over 1 h while the ink gels.
Undertake in situ amplitude and frequency measurements on gelled samples.
Select oscillatory test from the user options.
Select amplitude sweep and input parameters for an amplitude sweep test that is strain-controlled: 0.01 to 500%, at a constant 1 Hz frequency.
Load a new sample and select oscillatory test from the user options.
Select frequency test, and input frequency parameters between 0.01 and 10 Hz and a strain within the linear viscoelastic region (LVR) determined from amplitude sweep data.
Launch CAD Software to start the generation of a CAD model.
Select Tools | Materials in the CAD software to define printing parameters for the chosen bioink.
Input estimated filament diameter (~200-500 µm) in thickness tab to determine Z thickness of each layer.
Increase thickness value if delamination occurs, reduce thickness if resolution loss is observed.
Design desired structure layer by layer using Layer tabs in the software.
Group layers using Group tab and assign each layer to a level on the Z plane using Level tab.
Create one layer with filaments along x axis and a second layer with filaments along y axis for lattice structure.
Determine build height by selecting number of repeated units in the structure under Group tab.
Click Generate tool to create G-code for design and view 3D render of structure.
Launch 3D Discovery human-machine interface (HMI) software to initiate printing process.
Assemble printhead according to manufacturer's instructions.
Mount microvalve to printhead and screw in chosen extrusion nozzle.
Calibrate printhead using Needle Length Measurement function.
Load a culture vessel onto the printing platform.
Aliquot the bioink into the printing cartridge.
Screw the printing cartridge into the printhead above the micro-valve.
Connect the assembled printhead to the pneumatic pressure system.
Select the printhead on the HMI to engage.
Click check pressure to allow tuning of the extrusion pressure.
Once an appropriate pressure has been selected, open the G-code generated previously.
Click Run to initiate the printing process.

Culture human dermal fibroblasts (HDFs) and adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) in DMEM supplemented with fetal bovine serum (FBS), HEPES buffer, and penicillin/streptomycin until 90% confluency is reached.
Culture human epidermal keratinocytes (HEKs) in keratinocyte growth media (KGM) until 70%-80% confluency is reached.
Keep all cells under conditions of 37 °C, 5% CO2, and 95% air in an incubator during culture.
Wash the cells by gently pipetting 3 mL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) into flasks.
Tilt the flask to swirl the PBS over the cells.
Aspirate the PBS carefully without disturbing the attached cells.
Pipette 3 mL of 1x cell dissociation enzyme into the flask to cover the cells.
Place the flask in an incubator for 3 min.
Firmly tap the flask against the palm of the hand to dislodge the cells.
Neutralize the action of the enzyme using 6 mL of complete DMEM.
Incubate for a further 2 min if the cells remain attached after tapping.
Pipette cell suspensions into separate 15 mL tubes.
Take 10 µL from each tube for cell counting using a hemocytometer.
Centrifuge the remaining cell suspensions at 300 × g for 5 min to pellet the cells.
Aspirate the supernatant, being careful not to disturb the pellet.
Add the appropriate polymer solution (prepared in step 2.2).
Mix using gentle stimulation by pipetting.
Pipette 5 × 10^5 ADSCs mL^-1 per 1:1 collagen to pectin blend for the adipose layer.
Pipette 3 × 10^6 HDFs mL^-1 per 2:1 collagen to pectin blend for the papillary layer.
Pipette 1.5 × 10^6 HDFs mL^-1 per 2:1 collagen to pectin blend for the reticular layer.
Load each bioink into a separate cartridge.
Print the construct in the supporting fluid gel in a glass Petri dish according to section 4 instructions.
Inject 2 mL of 200 mM CaCl2·2H2O around the construct using a syringe and needle.
Inject 3 mL of adipogenic media into the fluid gel using a syringe and needle.
Remove the construct from the support bath using a spatula.
Gently wash the construct in PBS.
Culture the construct for 14 days in adipogenic medium in a 6-well plate.
Create an air-liquid interface at the surface of the construct by removing excess medium.
Seed 2 × 10^6 keratinocytes atop the construct to create an epidermal layer.
Culture further for 1 week prior to analysis.
